description: Stamp full business lineage (issue/epic/workflow-run/stage) into CloudEvents envelope extensions at every producer, raise EventCatalog to the per-type required-attribute registry that guards the matrix, and reconcile all issueno/epicno readers to the unified protocol names.

tasks.title: Raise EventCatalog to the per-type lineage registry with a conformance helper
tasks.description: Turn EventCatalog from the flat All name list into the protocol registry: every registered type declares the lineage attributes its envelope MUST always carry, grouped by family so workflow.stage.*/task.*/check.*/feedback.requested inherit the workflow.* base plus stage. Preserve the existing All list as a derived introspection surface so current callers keep compiling. Add a conformance helper (e.g. EventCatalog.RequiredAttributes(type) plus a test-side EnvelopeConformance.AssertRequired(envelope, type)) that fails when an emitted envelope is missing any required attribute. Declaration is the single source of truth the producers (T-002..T-006) stamp against and that the distributed conformance assertions call.
acceptanceCriteria: EventCatalog exposes, for every registered type, the set of always-required lineage attributes matching the matrix: workflow.run.* -> {projectid, workflowrunid}; workflow.stage.*/task.*/check.*/feedback.requested -> {projectid, workflowrunid, stage}; issue.* -> {projectid, issueid, issue}; epic.* -> {projectid, epicid}; agent-session.* -> {projectid, sessionid}; runner.* -> {runnerid}; com.mohist.inbox.item-persisted -> {projectid, issueid, issue}.

Catalog-only types with no producer today (runner.disconnected, workflow.repair-scheduled) are declared in the registry with their matrix required attributes but are not exercised by the conformance check.

Conditional/affiliation-dependent attributes (issueid/issue/epicid on workflow.*, epicid on issue.*, agentid/issue/workflowrunid/stage on agent-session.*) are modelled as conditional and validated by the stamping scenarios in the producer tasks, not as always-required.

A unit test proves the helper: a synthetic envelope of a registered type carrying all required attributes passes, and one missing a required attribute fails (negative case proving the guard actually catches drift).
Existing callers of EventCatalog.All still compile; the build passes with TreatWarningsAsErrors (`npm test` server track).
tasks.output: packages/server/src/Mohist.Server/Infrastructure/Events/EventCatalog.cs (registry + RequiredAttributes), the conformance helper, and a unit test with a passing positive and a failing negative case.
tasks.notes: Authoritative matrix lives here first; T-002..T-006 stamp to match and assert via the helper. Keep the matrix inside EventCatalog (D4) — do not introduce a second LineageMatrix class.

tasks.title: Stamp workflow-run identity and stage lineage in WorkflowRunStore
tasks.description: Extend WorkflowRunStore.ToCloudEvent to stamp workflowrunid (always) and issue/issueid from run annotations, plus epicid from the run's persisted lineage snapshot, and to stamp stage by structural inspection of the WorkflowEvent union variants that expose a Stage member (Stage*, StageApproval*, FeedbackRequested, Task*, Check*), not by bus-type prefix. Stamping stays inside the existing append transaction and derives everything from producer-owned state — no issue/epic aggregate load. Absent affiliations are omitted, never empty.
acceptanceCriteria: A workflow.run.* event whose annotations carry project id, issue id, and issue number stamps projectid, issueid, issue, and workflowrunid; the existing conditional-extensions path (only stamp when something is present) is preserved.
A workflow.* event for a run with no issue annotation omits issueid and issue while still carrying projectid and workflowrunid (no empty values).

Stage/task/check events stamp stage set to the stage name in addition to the workflow.* lineage; FeedbackRequested (typed workflow.feedback.requested) also stamps stage because it is structurally stage-bearing; WorkflowArtifactRecorded does not stamp stage because it carries no Stage member (D2).
WorkflowRunStore issues no cross-aggregate query (no issue/epic load) to stamp lineage.

TransactionalEventAppendSpecs (workflow) is updated to assert the new keys, the absent-annotation omission case, and that every emitted envelope satisfies EventCatalog.RequiredAttributes for its type via the conformance helper.
Server build + `npm test` pass.
tasks.output: packages/server/src/Mohist.Server/Infrastructure/Data/Workflow/WorkflowRunStore.cs updated; TransactionalEventAppendSpecs extended with lineage + stage assertions and conformance checks.
tasks.notes: Pattern-match the unwrapped WorkflowEvent variants to decide stage carriage (WorkflowEvent.cs lists which variants carry Stage). Use StringComparer.Ordinal for the extensions dict (already the convention here).

tasks.title: Stamp issue lineage from its producer-owned EpicId snapshot
tasks.description: In IssueStore rename the stamped issue number from issueno to issue (the protocol name users will write in expressions). Add a nullable EpicId property to the Issue aggregate plus an idempotent SetEpicId transition. Persist the producer-owned snapshot in Issues.EpicId as part of the Issue transaction and never replace Issue state from an Epic transaction. Stamp epicid from Issue state with no cross-aggregate query and omit it when the snapshot is null. T-004 delivers the affiliation through durable Epic-event reactions. Keep stamping a production-time snapshot; do not rewrite history on later relationship changes.
acceptanceCriteria: An issue.* event stamps projectid, issueid, and issue (the issue number); no issueno key is present.
An issue.* event for an issue whose persisted lineage snapshot carries a non-null EpicId additionally stamps epicid; an issue with a null snapshot omits epicid entirely (no empty value).

IssueStore hydrates Issue.EpicId on load; on save, epicid, serialized state, and the scalar projection all come from the Issue aggregate's current snapshot, with no query against db.EpicIssues or any other aggregate.

Issue exposes a nullable EpicId and an idempotent SetEpicId transition; IIssueGrain.SetEpicAffiliationAsync commits the local snapshot through IssueStore without recording a second membership event, since the authoritative EpicIssueLinked/EpicIssueUnlinked events live on the epic stream.
IssueStore persists the Issue snapshot and appends the Issue's own events in one transaction; no Epic or WorkflowRun state participates in that transaction.

IssueTransactionalEventAppendSpecs asserts issue (not issueno), epicid presence when state.EpicId is set and absence when null, and that each emitted envelope satisfies EventCatalog.RequiredAttributes for its type.
Server build + `npm test` pass.
tasks.output: packages/server/src/Mohist.Server/Issue/Domain/Issue.cs (EpicId + SetEpicId), packages/server/src/Mohist.Server/Issue/Grains/IIssueGrain.cs + IssueGrain.cs (SetEpicAffiliationAsync), packages/server/src/Mohist.Server/Infrastructure/Data/Issue/IssueStore.cs (rename + epicid stamp from state); IssueTransactionalEventAppendSpecs extended.
tasks.notes: Issue.EpicId is the Issue aggregate's locally applied affiliation revision, while EpicIssueRow remains membership truth. A durable Epic event reaction commands Issue after the Epic transaction commits; Issue then propagates its saved revision to WorkflowRun in a separate command. Historical event rows keep issueno (Non-Goal: no event backfill); read-side fallback is handled in T-007.

tasks.title: Drop epicno and propagate lineage through durable aggregate commands
tasks.description: Two Epic changes. (1) Stamp epic.* events with only projectid and epicid, removing epicno, and commit every Epic state transition with its Epic domain events in the same Epic transaction. (2) For lineage propagation (D5), link/unlink/status commands update only Epic-owned state and emit durable Epic events. Their handlers re-resolve current affiliation from the committed membership read model and send an idempotent command to Issue; Issue saves its own snapshot, then sends its saved lineage revision to WorkflowRun, whose own transaction applies it. Backfill current snapshots during schema migration without rewriting historical events.
acceptanceCriteria: An epic.* event stamps projectid and epicid and contains no epicno key.
Every Epic state mutation and its Epic domain events commit together; no best-effort post-commit Epic event append remains.

A unit test (on the extracted helper, no silo required) asserts projectid+epicid present and epicno absent, and that the produced extensions satisfy EventCatalog.RequiredAttributes for an epic.* type.
Link, unlink, terminal, and reopen transactions write only Epic-owned state and Epic events; they never write or lock Issue or WorkflowRun state.

After commit, Epic commands may send the same idempotent Issue command for latency; durable Epic handlers re-resolve the current affiliation on every delivery and retry if Issue or WorkflowRun propagation fails.
Issue and WorkflowRun apply lineage in their own transactions using the monotonic Issue lineage revision, so duplicate or delayed deliveries cannot overwrite a newer snapshot.
Existing Issue and WorkflowRun JSON epic ids are copied into the new snapshots at cutover; no historical event is rewritten.
Server build + `npm test` pass.
tasks.output: EpicGrain commits only Epic state/events; durable Epic subscription handlers propagate current affiliation through IIssueGrain.SetEpicAffiliationAsync and WorkflowRun lineage commands; one-time migration backfills current snapshots; Epic extension helper is unit-tested.
tasks.notes: The Epic transaction is the consistency boundary for EpicRow, membership rows, active-membership rows, and Epic events only. Producer snapshots let IssueStore and WorkflowRunStore stamp from their own state without membership lookup. Link/unlink entry points are LinkIssueAsync/LinkIssuesAsync/UnlinkIssueAsync/UnlinkIssuesAsync; terminal/reopen status events also trigger re-resolution for retained memberships.

tasks.title: Project AgentSession lineage from Metadata.Labels in AgentSessionStore
tasks.description: Replace the current extensions: null in AgentSessionStore.ToCloudEvent by projecting the session's own Metadata.Labels onto extensions: projectid (mohist.io/project-id), sessionid (the session id), agentid (mohist.io/agent-id) when agent-origin, and issue/workflowrunid/stage (mohist.io/issue-number / mohist.io/source-id / mohist.io/stage) when the session originates from a workflow/issue. Absent labels are omitted, never empty. Stamping uses only the session's own metadata — no cross-aggregate query.
acceptanceCriteria: An agent-session.* event whose labels carry project id, agent id, and an agent source kind stamps projectid, sessionid, and agentid.
A workflow/issue-origin session additionally stamps issue, workflowrunid, and stage from its labels; a session without those labels omits them (no empty values).
No cross-aggregate query is issued to stamp; all values come from Metadata.Labels (the session's own metadata).

AgentSessionTransactionalEventAppendSpecs is updated: the current 'projectid is NOT present' assertion is replaced by assertions that projectid/sessionid (and agentid/issue/workflowrunid/stage when labelled) are stamped, that absent labels are omitted, and that each envelope satisfies EventCatalog.RequiredAttributes for its type.
Server build + `npm test` pass.
tasks.output: packages/server/src/Mohist.Server/Infrastructure/Data/Sessions/AgentSessionStore.cs updated; AgentSessionTransactionalEventAppendSpecs updated for lineage projection + conformance.
tasks.notes: Label key constants live in packages/server/src/Mohist.Server/Sessions/Services/AgentSessionQueryMetadataKeys.cs (mohist.io/project-id, mohist.io/issue-number, mohist.io/source-id, mohist.io/stage, mohist.io/source-kind) and packages/server/src/Mohist.Server/Sessions/Services/GenericAgentSessionMetadata.cs (mohist.io/agent-id). The existing spec explicitly documents extensions: null as intentional (design OQ3) — that assertion is being superseded by this change.

tasks.title: Lift issue lineage in the inbox-synthesized event and reconcile its own issueno read
tasks.description: In InboxProjectionHandler, synthesize com.mohist.inbox.item-persisted with projectid plus issue and issueid lifted from the InboxItemPersistedHint already held in scope (no extra lookup). In the same file, update ResolveFromIssueExtensions to read the issue number from the issue key (with an issueno fallback so historical rows that were never backfilled still resolve), since IssueStore now stamps issue.
acceptanceCriteria: The synthesized inbox.item-persisted envelope stamps projectid, issueid, and issue from the hint payload (no additional lookup).
ResolveFromIssueExtensions resolves the issue number from the issue key, falling back to issueno for pre-change historical rows, and still returns null when neither is parseable.
A spec covering the inbox synthesis path asserts projectid/issueid/issue are stamped and that the envelope satisfies EventCatalog.RequiredAttributes for com.mohist.inbox.item-persisted.
Server build + `npm test` pass.
tasks.output: packages/server/src/Mohist.Server/Events/Subscriptions/InboxProjectionHandler.cs updated (synthesis stamping + dual-key read); inbox synthesis spec extended.
tasks.notes: Synthesis site is InboxProjectionHandler.cs:148-167; the issueno read is at :213. The InboxItemPersistedHint already carries IssueId/IssueNumber. The issueno fallback is the permanent history shim (Non-Goal forbids backfill).

tasks.title: Reconcile issueno/epicno readers (server handlers + web) to the unified names
tasks.description: Update the remaining read-side consumers that key on the legacy names so lineage resolution stays consistent with the stamped names. EpicAutoDoneHandler and HermesIssueNotificationHandler read issue (with an issueno fallback for historical rows). The web envelope reader and any fixtures/docs referencing issueno or epicno move to issue / epicid. This lands in the same change as the producer rename so producers and consumers never disagree on the key (D3).
acceptanceCriteria: EpicAutoDoneHandler (the two issueno reads in EpicProgressRecomputeDispatcher) resolves the issue number from issue, falling back to issueno for historical rows.
HermesIssueNotificationHandler.ResolveFromIssueExtensions reads issue with an issueno fallback.
packages/web event-envelope.ts documents issue (and epicid) instead of issueno/epicno; any web code/fixtures hardcoding issueno or epicno are updated to issue / epicid.
Server build + `npm test` pass; web `npm run typecheck -w packages/web` and `npm run test:run -w packages/web` pass.

After T-003 (issueno -> issue producer) and T-004 (epicno drop) land, no producer or consumer references issueno as the primary key or references epicno anywhere; only the intentional history-fallback reads remain.
tasks.output: EpicAutoDoneHandler.cs, HermesIssueNotificationHandler.cs, and packages/web/src/app/providers/model/event-envelope.ts (+ fixtures) reconciled to issue/epicid with history fallback where rows are traversed.
tasks.notes: Ship the rename atomically (D3): web only reads issue after the server stamps it. T-003 produces the issue rename and T-004 drops epicno, so T-007 depends on both before its end-state AC can hold; T-006 already handled InboxProjectionHandler's own read in the same file. Keep the dual-key issueno fallback minimal and permanent in history-traversing handlers (Non-Goal: no backfill).
